title: U.S. House · Minnesota's 5th District
area: Minneapolis and surrounding Hennepin County suburbs, including Saint Louis Park, Richfield and parts of Bloomington and Brooklyn Park.

context.text: Incumbent Ilhan Omar (D) won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary with 80.7% of the vote against four challengers. John Nagel won the Republican primary with 52.2% against three challengers. DeVelle Jackson is running as an independent.

candidates.name: Ilhan Omar
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary with 80.7% of the vote.

priorities.text: Abolish U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), citing deaths in ICE custody and due-process concerns in immigration courts.

Lower prescription drug costs, cap child care costs at 7% of income, expand rental assistance, provide $20,000 in down-payment assistance for first-time homebuyers, and make college and trade school tuition-free.
End what she calls 'forever wars' and require congressional authorization for military action, prioritizing diplomacy and human rights in foreign policy.

positions.summary: Supports abolishing ICE rather than expanding immigration enforcement.
positions.quote: There is no reforming an agency that will ignore the Constitution and kill Americans and prevent any meaningful investigation into their deaths. ICE must be abolished.

positions.summary: Supports replacing for-profit health insurance with Medicare for All.
positions.quote: replacing for-profit health insurance with Medicare For All

positions.summary: Supports a wealth tax on billionaires as part of the Progressive Caucus agenda she helps advance.
Backs capping child care costs at 7% of household income.
positions.quote: cap child care costs at 7% of income

positions.summary: Supports environmental justice initiatives as part of addressing the climate crisis.
Supports expanding rental assistance to address housing costs.

record.text: Serves on the House Budget Committee and the Education and Workforce Committee in the 119th Congress; is the lead Democrat on the Workforce Protections Subcommittee.
Serves as Deputy Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus.
Introduced the Make ICE Pay Act, announced September 17, 2026, following 'Operation Metro Surge' immigration enforcement activity in Minnesota.
Spoke at a September 22, 2026 House Oversight and Government Reform Committee hearing on deaths in DHS custody, alongside family members of people who died during immigration enforcement encounters.

candidates.name: John Nagel
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary with 52.2% of the vote.

priorities.text: Cut federal spending and taxes, and reduce what he calls government waste and intrusiveness.
Support law enforcement funding and back Attorney General efforts against violent crime.
Secure the U.S.-Mexico border and support the Trump administration's border enforcement approach.

statements.quote: In Congress, I will fight to make sure our border is locked down so tightly that Democrats can never tear it open again.
statements.context: On his campaign website's immigration page

statements.quote: our men and women in blue receive the funding and support they deserve

candidates.researchNotes: Statements come from his campaign website issues section and press page; his site lists issues in short paragraphs, with no stated position found on abortion, guns, rent, minimum wage, climate or other guide issues beyond those listed. His website says he supports legal immigration and faster processing; it does not address deportations.

candidates.name: DeVelle Jackson

priorities.text: Reduce the two-party system's control over political access, arguing elected officials should answer to voters rather than party establishments.

Strengthen privacy and data-rights protections against government and corporate surveillance, including limits on facial recognition, geofencing, and government purchase of personal data to bypass warrant requirements.
Pair direct affordability relief with policies to expand housing supply, domestic production, and job training rather than relief alone.

positions.summary: Supports restoring in federal law the viability framework associated with Roe v. Wade and Planned Parenthood v. Casey.
positions.quote: I support restoring in federal law the core viability framework associated with Roe v. Wade and reaffirmed in Planned Parenthood v. Casey.

positions.summary: Supports comprehensive federal gun legislation with multiple points of intervention, while stating the Second Amendment right is not unlimited.
positions.quote: I support comprehensive federal gun legislation that preserves the individual Second Amendment right to keep and bear arms as a constitutional safeguard of a free people, including lawful self-defense, hunting, and sporting use, while recognizing that the right is not unlimited.

positions.summary: Supports a tax on billionaires and the ultra-wealthy with a steeper top income-tax rate and action on corporate loopholes.
positions.quote: I support a Rich Tax on billionaires and the ultra-wealthy, with a steeper income-tax curve at the very top and stronger action against offshore tax avoidance and corporate loopholes.

positions.summary: Supports a universal healthcare guarantee centered on a national public option.
positions.quote: I support a universal healthcare guarantee that builds upon Medicare, Medicaid, veterans' care, employer and union plans, private insurance, and successful state programs.

positions.summary: Says he will defend Congress's war powers and that military action should have lawful authorization.
positions.quote: I will defend Congress's war powers and oppose unauthorized, open-ended, and forever conflicts.

candidates.researchNotes: Candidate has a campaign website with a 12-point platform (jacksonforcongress.us) in addition to his Ballotpedia survey; positions and statements come from the platform page. No stated position found on school choice, minimum wage, tariffs, child care or police funding.

statements.quote: Immigration enforcement does not place federal agents above the law or authorize occupation tactics in American neighborhoods.
statements.context: On his campaign website's platform page

statements.quote: I support clean, renewable energy and strong federal action against pollution and the misuse of shared resources.
statements.context: On his campaign website's platform page

statements.quote: Federal policy should prevent eviction, move people quickly from shelters or the street into permanent housing, and provide supportive housing for people who need continuing services.
statements.context: On his campaign website's platform page

statements.quote: That means making it easier to build, produce, hire, train, and compete while ensuring working people share in the value they create.
statements.context: On his campaign website; Ballotpedia-quoted text

sources.title: United States House of Representatives elections in Minnesota, 2026
